channel.title: Not Enough Time
channel.description: A curated summary of contemporary frontier discussions.

item.title: Wall Street hits its limit on AI debt
item.description: Wall Street strategists warn that AI data center borrowing is hitting credit limits. Anthropic's public filing splits investors over whether frontier AI labs build lasting moats. Autonomous AI hackers cut corporate breach costs to pennies and outpace human defenders. Lean open models and phone chips threaten to bypass giant AI data centers. AI coding agents shrink software startups while creating costly testing and database bottlenecks.

item.title: Corporate buyers balk at frontier AI costs
item.description: Investors warn that the AI data center boom rests on fragile startup spending. Corporate buyers expect cheap open-weight AI models to take most routine work. Venture investors warn that AI coding tools will crush per-seat software margins. AI shopping bots steer wealthy buyers to pricier goods while retailers block checkouts. Automated AI hacks push Washington to license private cyber strikes on scam cartels.

item.title: AI hits limits on money, chips and security
item.description: Banks are locking AI assistants out of customer accounts. Lenders and factory limits choke off the race to build AI data centers. AI-powered hacking is exposing old software flaws faster than companies can fix them.

item.title: AI computing power becomes a traded commodity
item.description: AI is squeezing traditional software profits and changing how engineers get paid. Crypto money shifts from startups to tradable tokens, and traditional finance pushes back. Traders are turning AI computing hours into a financial commodity like oil.
